entities.name: PMID:25426379
observations: Onishi et al. reported daily topical bFGF versus saline after induction of secondary lymphedema in rat tails.
Topical bFGF reduced tail volume, accelerated indocyanine-green fluorescence decline, and reduced tissue areas relative to saline.
At postoperative day 14, bFGF increased VEGF-C mRNA/protein and histologic lymphatic-vessel density.
The study did not establish necessity of lymphangiogenesis using pathway blockade or ablation.

entities.name: bFGF/FGF2
observations: Daily topical administration improved secondary lymphedema-related outcomes in a rat-tail model.
The retrieved evidence does not verify formulation, concentration, amount, or application area.

entities.name: Secondary lymphedema
observations: In a rat-tail injury/obstruction model, topical bFGF improved tail volume, lymphatic drainage-associated ICG fluorescence, and tissue-area outcomes versus saline.
The improvement coincided with VEGF-C induction and increased lymphatic-vessel density.
Mechanistic causality remains suggestive rather than definitive because no pathway-inhibition experiment was reported.

entities.name: VEGF-C
observations: Topical bFGF increased VEGF-C mRNA and protein at postoperative day 14 in the rat-tail secondary lymphedema model.

entities.name: Lymphangiogenic bFGF benefit
observations: Topical bFGF improved secondary lymphedema while increasing VEGF-C and lymphatic-vessel density, supporting a lymphangiogenic mechanism.
The parallel changes do not prove that lymphangiogenesis is required for the benefit.

entities.name: Trisomy 18
observations: Edwards syndrome commonly causes craniofacial dysmorphism, limb abnormalities, renal anomalies, growth restriction, and severe neonatal respiratory compromise.
The diagnosis is confirmed by demonstrating an extra chromosome 18, classically with conventional karyotyping.

entities.name: Edwards phenotype
observations: A premature neonate with oligohydramnios, dysmorphic facies, limb asymmetry/great-toe displacement, and bilateral hydroureteronephrosis has a pattern suggestive of trisomy 18.
Conventional karyotyping is the definitive test among the choices when a recognizable whole-chromosome aneuploidy is suspected.
